NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday mounted another attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his Diwali visit to Chhattisgarh's Bastar, a region once notorious for the presence of Naxalites Firing a fresh salvo over PM Modi's "dimagi naxal" remark during his visit, the Congress leader repeated his challenge for the Prime Minister to debate him over "who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces".Tagging CRPF on his X post, the Rae Bareli MP also wrote: "Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals."Rahul was responding to PM Modi's claim that "Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over".During his visit to Bastar on Sunday, PM Modi made a big assertion saying "while armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations"."We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations.We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," PM Modi was quoted as saying by the news agency ANI, which Rahul rebutted on Monday.PM Modi further said the Maoist terror elimination was a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will.“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ (their ideological supporters) have taken control of several organisations,” he said. “Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added.On his Independence Day in August, PM Modi had also referred to ‘dimagi Naxals’, saying the country succeeded in removing armed Naxalism, but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, PM Modi on Sunday said it was not easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 states were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill. Thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, with around 2,000 Naxal attacks taking place annually, he said.“This land had become soaked in blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments.
Article Summary: Rahul was responding to PM Modi's claim that "Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over" The Congress leader repeated his challenge for the Prime Minister to debate him over "who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces"

Article Title: 'Semantically ignorant': Congress defends Kharge's 'Diwali a khushiyon ki Eid' remark
Article Text:
"Those making a big deal out of Kharge ji’s statement are semantically ignorant," Congress leader Pawan Khera said.

Congress hits back at BJP

BJP questions comparison with Eid

NEW DELHI: The Congress and the BJP traded barbs over AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge 's description of Diwali as "khushiyon ka Eid", with the opposition party accusing the ruling party of deliberately misinterpreting his festive greeting.The row began after Kharge used the phrase while wishing people on Diwali over the weekend. The BJP objected to the comparison, arguing that Diwali should be referred to by its own name and accusing the Congress of being anti-Sanatani.BJP national media co-in-charge and spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari alleged that the Congress had brought vote-bank politics into Diwali celebrations by describing the festival as an "Eid of Happiness".Responding to the criticism, Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said the BJP leaders had misunderstood the meaning of the word Eid."Those making a big deal out of Kharge ji’s statement are semantically ignorant," Khera said as per news agency PTI."The word 'Eid' literally means 'festival'. Now go and listen to his statement again. It is perfectly normal -- unlike the Sanghi negativity that makes some people incapable of sparing even a festival," Khera said on X.He also launched a sharp attack on those criticising Kharge, urging them to understand the meaning of the phrase rather than turn it into a controversy."In the spirit of Diwali and for the love of God, please light a bulb or two in your brain as well, and spare the rest of us the public display of your stupidity. Jaahil kahin ke (they are illiterates)," Khera added.BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia questioned why Kharge had compared Diwali, which he described as the biggest festival of Hindus, with Eid."Mr Kharge, what exactly is the problem with calling Diwali, the biggest festival of Hindus, by its own name?"Bhatia said Eid and Diwali each had their own religious significance and distinct traditions. He also challenged Kharge and Rahul Gandhi to explain whether they would describe Eid as the "Diwali of joy"."Has changing the identity of Hindu festivals become a matter of political etiquette in Congress's so-called secularism? Rahul Gandhi and Mr Kharge, answer this: will you ever have the courage to call Eid the "Diwali of joy," he asked."Respect Hindus' faith; don't change the identity of their festivals. Diwali was, Diwali is, and Diwali will remain Diwali," Bhatia said.Another BJP spokesperson, Tuhin Sinha , also criticised the Congress, saying Muslims celebrate Eid twice a year while the party wanted to describe every Hindu festival as "Khushiyon ki Eid".
Article Summary: AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge used the phrase while wishing people on Diwali over the weekend. The BJP objected to the comparison and accused the Congress of being anti-Sanatani. Congress leader Pawan Khera said the BJP leaders had misunderstood the meaning of the word Eid.

Article Title: 'No impact on India-US ties': Tharoor says Trump retains power on tariffs, Iran war

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict."Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war. All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days. However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign."Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations. He said President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback. He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin.

NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired about his health. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups.The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. The meeting comes amid signs of internal discord within the party, adding a political dimension to Patel’s hospital visit.Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday night with a respiratory and chest infection, after being discharged from Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic. Dr Pratit Samdani, a doctor at the hospital, said on Thursday that Pawar was stable and undergoing treatment."Sharad Pawar was admitted yesterday at Breach Candy Hospital for a respiratory and chest infection. He is stable and under treatment. He was admitted last night; he had a cough and an infection, something like bronchitis trouble. His treatment is ongoing, and he is currently stable," Dr Samdani told reporters.After meeting Pawar, Patel said the hospital admission was part of his routine medical check-ups and that his health was good. He also dismissed speculation that their meeting involved political discussions, saying he continued to meet Pawar and his daughter, Supriya Sule, because of their family ties.Also read: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad Pawar In a post on X, Patel said, "I visited the Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai to pay a courtesy call on the esteemed Shri Sharad Pawar Saheb and inquired about his health."Providing an update on Pawar's condition, Patel said, "Sharad Pawar due to fatigue two days ago, was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune for a checkup. After that, he came to Mumbai, and here his health is fine. Naturally, a checkup happens once or twice a year, for a complete checkup, so in that context only he is admitted here at Breach Candy. His health is good. I am also happy that I came here, but everything is fine, and sahab was also in good spirits. He was asking about what is happening in politics in the country and state, as that is his interest. We had a good conversation, and I am happy that in a day or two all his checkups will be completed, so he will return home soon so he can rest."Patel also commented on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conversation with Pawar, describing their relationship as long-standing and cordial. He said Modi's call to enquire about Pawar's health was natural given their association over the years.“Sharad Pawar and Narendra Modi have had a very long-standing relationship. I have also known Modi ji for many years and personally know about the relationship between him and Pawar sahab... I have witnessed their very good, cordial and respectful relationship over the years, even when we were in the UPA government in Delhi, and Modi ji was the Chief Minister of Gujarat... Modi ji is such a senior leader of the country today. So, if he received information about Sharad Pawar ji's health, it was natural for him to enquire about his well-being and speak to him...”Earlier, Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 after complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. According to a statement issued by Dr Purvez K Grant, Chief Cardiologist, Chairman and Managing Trustee of the hospital, Pawar was stable and doing well at the time of his discharge."Mr Sharad Pawar has been discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai. We wish him good health and a speedy recovery," the statement said.His daughter, Baramati MP and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule, had earlier said that Pawar was undergoing medical tests and that his health parameters were stable. Ruby Hall Clinic subsequently said he would remain under observation as a precautionary measure. Doctors cleared him for discharge after his condition remained stable and his discomfort subsided.The developments come amid growing concerns within the BJP over organisational differences in its ally -- NCP. Union home minister Amit Shah met several senior NCP functionaries late Sunday who are believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and urged them to resolve their differences in the party’s interest.Those who met Shah included NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra unit chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and leaders Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth were absent from the meeting.Following the meeting, Sunetra Pawar convened a core committee meeting in Mumbai.
Article Summary: NCP leader Praful Patel visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups. The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar's leadership.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said that while armed Naxalites had been eliminated from the forests, the threat of Naxalism was not over, claiming that "Dimagi Naxals" had taken control of several organisations including political parties.Addressing security personnel while celebrating Diwali at a Central Reserve Police Force ( CRPF ) camp in Karanpur in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district, PM Modi said the country needed to identify and defeat such elements to ensure national security."We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. While armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," he said.The prime minister's remarks come months after the Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism following the elimination of several Maoist leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.PM Modi described the elimination of Maoist terror as a victory for the government's policies and political will. He said his government had taken decisions that dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and separatists, while giving security forces greater freedom to respond to attacks."Earlier governments had tied the hands of security forces in the fight on the ground. Maoist attacks took place, but security forces did not have the freedom to retaliate effectively. We gave security forces the freedom to take all necessary decisions," he said.He also said the government had worked to dismantle the support networks that Left-Wing Extremism received from within the administration and the system.PM Modi said the government's objective was to ensure that no family lost a child to Maoist violence and no young person was forced to take up arms. He added that sustained security operations, alongside development initiatives, had helped win the trust of people in Naxal-affected areas.Recalling the scale of the challenge, the prime minister said more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states had once been affected by Naxalism. He also pointed out that, for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel had been killed in the line of duty over the past year.
Article Summary: PM Modi said the country needed to identify and defeat such elements to ensure national security. The Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism. PM Modi described the elimination of Maoist terror as a victory for the government's policies and political will.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee joined Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee in a protest in Kolkata’s Kalighat. She accused the BJP of hooliganism and alleged a breakdown of law and order in the state.She said she had written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over the incident.The protest followed an overnight confrontation outside Abhishek’s residence, where clashes reportedly broke out between TMC workers and BJP supporters around 2am. Abhishek alleged that BJP workers attacked his residence after conducting reconnaissance of the premises for two days.He later claimed that the confrontation continued until 7am, accused police personnel of failing to stop the attackers and alleged that some officers were assaulted while trying to intervene. Several people were reportedly injured, while police imposed prohibitory restrictions around the residence and detained some people.BJP rejected the allegations, blaming the confrontation on a birthday gathering organised on a public road.The incident has since triggered a political war of words, with leaders from both sides trading accusations over the violence and the state’s law-and-order situation.Mamata reached Abhishek’s Kalighat residence later on Saturday and joined the protest. She accused the BJP of creating disturbances in the area and alleged that a group of people had attacked a Kali Puja celebration.She also raised concerns over the arrangements for traditional pujas ahead of Kali Puja and Diwali. Mamata claimed that permissions for some long-standing puja celebrations had been revoked while a new puja was allowed to be organised on the main road.“Tomorrow is Kali Puja and Diwali. Last night, at 2:00 AM, an attack was carried out at Abhishek Banerjee’s house. This is our locality, a route through which many processions of Goddess Kali pass. Why are you causing such a disturbance? You have revoked permissions for our traditional, long-standing pujas while allowing new ones to be held instead,” she said.She alleged that the new puja arrangement had blocked access to their own celebration and accused the authorities of high-handedness. She also said she had written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over what she described as a breakdown of law and order.The confrontation reportedly began around 2am on Saturday, when BJP supporters allegedly raised slogans calling Abhishek a “chor” (thief) outside his Kalighat residence. TMC workers had gathered in the area. According to reports, the slogans were followed by counter-sloganeering, arguments and a clash between the two groups.The confrontation involved allegations of assault, stone-pelting and vandalism. Abhishek, who came out of his residence during the night to meet injured party workers, alleged that the attackers used wooden rods fitted with nails and vandalised a local TMC office.Police and party accounts put the duration of the initial clashes between 2am and 3.30am. Abhishek, however, later claimed that the confrontation continued until 7am.He alleged that four to five of his supporters sustained serious injuries. One of them, he said, required plastic surgery, while another suffered a fracture. Police sources said several people from both sides were injured. A separate report put the number of injured at eight, including three who were seriously hurt.The incident came hours after Abhishek raised allegations of surveillance outside his office and residence. On Friday, he claimed that unidentified individuals had been conducting reconnaissance of the premises for two consecutive days.He said the individuals claimed to be police personnel when confronted. Abhishek questioned why the state police were allegedly keeping watch on an elected MP’s residence and demanded an inquiry into who had authorised the surveillance and for what purpose.He tagged Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Kolkata Police, West Bengal Police and the Union Home Ministry in his post, seeking an investigation to establish the identities of those involved.Hours later, he alleged that his residence had been attacked by BJP workers. Sharing a video purportedly showing the incident, he wrote on X: “After two days of continuous recce, this is how BJP hooligans attacked my house at 2 am today. Watch the footage and see for yourself. If this is what can happen to an elected Member of Parliament, imagine the plight of the common man in WB.”PTI said it could not independently verify the authenticity of the video.Abhishek described the incident as the seventh attempt on his life in six months. He also accused the police and the judiciary of failing to act against those allegedly targeting him.Escalating his criticism after the confrontation, Abhishek alleged that police personnel present at the spot failed to prevent the violence. He claimed that some officers remained silent spectators, while others who tried to intervene were assaulted.“The attack continued till 7 am. Although the police were there, some of them acted as silent spectators, and others who tried to stop the BJP goons were beaten up by them,” he said.“The police who can’t protect themselves cannot protect the common people anyway,” he added.Abhishek also shared a video that he claimed showed a BJP worker slapping a plainclothes police officer. The TMC accused the BJP workers of assaulting police personnel and questioned why those involved had not been arrested.He said the incident showed how vulnerable ordinary people could be if police personnel themselves were unable to protect themselves. He also cited figures on alleged crimes in the state between May and October, claiming that around 2,500 rapes, 600 murders and more than 32,000 crimes had taken place during the period. These figures were claims made by Abhishek.The Kolkata Police said a commotion had broken out between supporters of the two parties and that a police team intervened. An investigation was underway, a police officer said, without providing further details.Prohibitory orders were imposed around Abhishek’s residence, barring gatherings of more than five people. A large police contingent was deployed in the area and several people were detained in connection with the incident.Police sources said people from both sides had been injured and the situation remained tense through the night.The BJP rejected Abhishek’s allegations and accused TMC supporters of provoking the confrontation by holding a birthday celebration on a public road.West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh dismissed the claims as an attempt to mislead people. He questioned why anyone would want to kill Abhishek and said a disturbance was bound to follow if a public space was occupied for a celebration.Union minister Sukanta Majumdar also criticised the decision to hold the gathering on a footpath. He said there was no objection to celebrating a birthday but argued that it should have been organised inside a residence or at a venue rather than on a public road.“If you block public roads in front of your house and hold a birthday celebration on the footpath, naturally people will get angry. The public is already upset with you; on top of that, if you behave like this, confrontations are bound to happen,” he said.Majumdar rejected allegations of BJP involvement and said the party did not want to “dirty its hands with small fry”.BJP leader Ritabrata Bandopadhyay also disputed the TMC’s account. He claimed local residents were angry because the gathering had obstructed roads used for transporting idols ahead of Kali Puja. He said the birthday celebration should have been held inside Abhishek’s residence.TMC MP Sougata Roy accused BJP workers of conducting a prior reconnaissance of the area before attacking Abhishek’s residence. He alleged that police personnel were present but failed to control the situation, and that some officers were also assaulted.Roy described the incident as an attempt to intimidate people and suppress the opposition.TMC MP Kirti Azad alleged that men armed with stones and sticks attacked the premises for 30 to 45 minutes. He claimed CCTV footage was available and accused the police of escorting those involved instead of arresting them.TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh also alleged that party workers were being targeted and questioned the police action following the incident. Party spokesperson and advocate Arka Nag described the episode as an alleged attempt to murder Abhishek and his supporters. He said the party had lodged a police complaint and questioned the imposition of prohibitory restrictions, arguing that they could affect the movement of Kali idols during the festival.The incident also drew reactions from leaders outside the two parties. Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury said nobody should be denied the right to celebrate a birthday. Congress leader Udit Raj described the incident as an unconstitutional act and an attack on democracy.Rashtriya Janata Dal MP Sudhakar Singh demanded President’s Rule in West Bengal, alleging that the state government had failed to maintain law and order.The confrontation comes against the backdrop of the BJP’s victory in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, which ended the TMC’s 15-year rule. The BJP is now in government, while the TMC, led by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee, is in opposition.The two parties have since traded allegations of violence and intimidation. The latest clash in Kalighat has added to the political tension in the state, with both sides blaming the other for the confrontation.With Kali Puja and Diwali approaching, the incident has also brought the arrangements for celebrations in Kalighat into the political dispute. Further details of the investigation and action against those detained are awaited.
Article Summary: Mamata Banerjee accuses the BJP of hooliganism and alleged a breakdown of law and order in the state. She said she had written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over the incident. The protest followed an overnight confrontation outside Abhishek’s residence.

He will go to Vidhan Sabha," he said.Earlier on Wednesday, AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi had also criticised the BJP and the Samajwadi Party (SP), asserting that Muslims would no longer be treated as mere vote banks but would emerge as political leaders and lawmakers in Uttar Pradesh.Citing El-Sayed's electoral success in the US, Owaisi argued that Muslims have long been subjected to stereotypes in Indian political discourse."Abdul won in Michigan. Did this not become an issue when I said something on it? People from the BJP used to mock and say, 'Abdul puncture banata hai' (Abdul repairs punctures). The SP people used to say, 'Abdul dari bicchayega' (Abdul will spread the carpets)," Owaisi told ANI.Pathan also accused the BJP of discriminating against Muslims over their religious practices, food habits and places of worship, alleging that the community had faced growing hostility under the party's rule."Since the BJP government came into power in the last 12 years, they have completely ruined the country. Today, the BJP government has launched an open war against the Muslims. They hate our prayers, hijab, food, mosques, madrasas, bulldozers, mob lynching of Muslims," he said.He also criticised opposition parties, including the Congress and the SP, accusing them of approaching Muslims for electoral support without addressing their social, economic and educational concerns."Both parties have used the Muslims only for votes. They have done nothing else," he said.Referring to the Mahmood Rahman Committee and the Ranganath Mishra Commission reports, Pathan said their findings highlighted the community's socio-economic backwardness."The report of the Mahmood Rahman Committee is scary. Look at the report of the Ranganath Mishra Committee. All the reports are a testimony to the fact that the Muslims are backward," he said.Questioning the response of political leaders to issues concerning Muslims in Uttar Pradesh, Pathan asked whether they had visited families affected by demolitions or reached out to Muslim leaders who had been jailed."When the Muslims were oppressed in madrasas, where they were bulldozed, did you ever go there? When Azam Khan went back to jail, did you go to meet him?" he asked."The people are watching. They will get an equal answer in the elections," he added.Pathan also referred to the debate over Muslim population growth, arguing that the community's total fertility rate (TFR) had declined over the years."These numbers show that the total fertility rate of Muslims is decreasing. In 1992-1993, the Muslim's TFR rate was 4.4. It decreased to 2.6 in 2015-16. After that, it decreased to 2.3 in 1921. So the TFR rate is decreasing," he said.He accused certain political leaders of spreading misinformation and hostility towards Muslims, referring to remarks by RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and a BJP MP on having three-four and four-five children."Why don't you stop them? And here, they are spreading lies. They are spreading hatred. They just want to defame the Muslims," he said.Urging people to refrain from making derogatory remarks against the community, Pathan said, "The people have become sensible. So stop talking nonsense."
Article Summary: AIMIM leader Waris Pathan has called for stronger Muslim political representation in Uttar Pradesh. NEW DELHI: Punjab Police, with the assistance of central agencies, has secured the deportation of wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia after a 10-month-long international manhunt under Operation SHAHID.Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav said on Sunday that the state government had announced a reward of Rs 5 lakh for information leading to the gangster's arrest.Announcing the development in a post on social media platform X, Yadav said the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) Punjab, in coordination with the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC) of Counter Intelligence, Punjab, and central agencies, coordinated the operation to bring Afridi back from Ethiopia."In a major breakthrough, Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) Punjab, in coordination with the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (#OFTEC) of Counter Intelligence, Punjab with the support of central agencies, secures the deportation of Gurwinder alias Afridi, a key kingpin of the Doni Bal-Prabh Dassuwal gang, from Ethiopia following a 10-month-long international manhunt under Operation SHAHID," the DGP said.According to Yadav, preliminary investigations indicate that Afridi was allegedly directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and other organised criminal activities in Punjab while operating from abroad.The operation involved sustained intelligence gathering, surveillance and tracking across several countries in Asia, South America and Africa, with the support of national and international agencies, he said.Yadav also acknowledged the role of the ministry of external affairs and other central agencies in facilitating the operation."We thank the ministry of external affairs and all other central agencies as part of this international cooperation," he said.The DGP reiterated that Punjab Police remains committed to dismantling gangster networks, curbing organised crime and maintaining peace and security across the state.

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has warned students and parents against falling victim to fake medical colleges, fraudulent admission offers and forged approval documents, following a Supreme Court case involving a purported medical college allegedly operating from a farmhouse.In an advisory, the medical regulator said some institutions were offering medical and allied courses without the requisite statutory approval or recognition. Misleading advertisements, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers could leave students and parents vulnerable to fraud, it cautioned.The warning follows the Supreme Court's intervention in Ayesha Jain vs Amity University, Noida & Others, in which it directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to alert students and parents against enrolling in institutions without first verifying their authenticity.The NMC has specifically cautioned that a college figuring on its official list does not necessarily mean it has permission to admit students for the current academic year. Students must check the college's approval for the relevant year and its sanctioned intake through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board records.It has also advised candidates not to rely on brochures, websites, advertisements or purported Letters of Permission circulated by institutions.Admissions should be pursued through official counselling channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee wherever applicable, or the respective state counselling authorities.The regulator has warned against making payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries. It has also clarified that approval or affiliation from another authority cannot be treated as NMC permission to run an MBBS course.Students can report suspected fake colleges, forged approval letters and fraudulent admission offers to the NMC, state medical education departments or local police.

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has described the imposition of the Emergency as a mistake, saying she believes her mother-in-law and then prime minister Indira Gandhi eventually came to regret the decision.The Congress leader in her upcoming book "Belonging: A Journey of Love" also writes that keeping Sanjay Gandhi "in check" could have prevented much of the damage that followed the imposition of the Emergency, according to her interview with The Guardian ahead of the book’s release."I always feel that Mrs (Indira) Gandhi was a democrat at heart," Sonia told the British daily. "I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her," she added.According to The Guardian, Sonia recalled that the decision to impose the Emergency divided the family.Her husband, Rajiv Gandhi , had reportedly advised his mother to wait until the next election, while Sanjay argued that the opposition would destroy her and had to be stopped.Sonia said the disagreement also created tensions within the family, as Rajiv tried to confront his mother but she refused to listen."Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed," she wrote in the book, according to The Guardian.In a separate interview with The Hindu, published on Saturday, Sonia said Sanjay was not the only person who influenced the decision.She pointed to pressure from some of Indira's senior colleagues and said few people around the then prime minister shared Rajiv's views."It was not only Sanjay, though in the public mind he is often seen as synonymous with the Emergency. There was a lot of pressure from some of her senior colleagues, and I think there were very few people around her like Rajiv who had a different point of view," she said."I think eventually my mother-in-law began to understand the situation through her own wisdom and took actions to remedy it," she added.Sonia said she became aware of the full gravity of the events only after the Emergency ended. While acknowledging that democratic rights had been curtailed and habeas corpus suspended, she said the measures had been taken constitutionally."It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," she said.Looking back, Sonia said Indira had been struggling to deal with the deteriorating situation at the time."Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Indira Gandhi's point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," she said.Sonia said hindsight helped put the events into perspective. She also pointed out that Indira later called elections and publicly expressed regret over the excesses committed during the Emergency."And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.In her interview with The Guardian, Sonia also recalled crying as she watched the Babri mosque being demolished in December 1992.She said the incident made her realise that the country faced "a long battle for the secular nation that Mahatma Gandhi, Nehru and their colleagues had strived to build", the British daily reported.Sonia also acknowledged that the Congress had, in part, contributed to the rise of the BJP and its hardline Hindutva politics."I think we have been too complacent in many ways. There was a laissez-faire kind of an attitude," she said.Indira Gandhi imposed the Emergency shortly before midnight on June 25, 1975. President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued the proclamation on her recommendation, and the Union Cabinet later ratified it.On January 18, 1977, Indira announced fresh Lok Sabha elections and released political prisoners. She and Sanjay Gandhi were defeated in the March 1977 elections. The Emergency officially ended on March 21, 1977.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi has described the imposition of the Emergency as a mistake. She believes her mother-in-law and then prime minister Indira Gandhi eventually came to regret the decision. Sonia also writes that keeping Sanjay Gandhi "in check" could have prevented much of the damage that followed the Emergency.

Article Title: After more than 400 trees were cut at Trump's Washington golf course, a federal judge names a former prosecutor to investigate whether government lawyers misled her about plans to continue redevelopme
Article Text:
Trump's golf course redevelopment faces scrutiny over environmental safeguards, public land and compliance with judicial orders.

Former prosecutor appointed to examine government conduct

The controversy surrounding the tree removal

Why Jessie Liu's appointment matters

A wider political and legal confrontation

A dispute over a public golf course in the heart of Washington DC has taken an unexpected turn, moving beyond questions of landscaping and redevelopment to the conduct of the federal government itself. What began as a legal challenge to President Donald Trump's plans to transform a historic recreational space has now prompted a judicial investigation into whether government lawyers misrepresented the administration's intentions. With hundreds of trees already removed and construction plans facing resistance, the case has become a test of how far the government can go when a court has ordered it to stop.According to the latest report by Reuters, US District Judge Ana Reyes announced on Saturday that she would appoint Jessie Liu, a former US attorney for the District of Columbia, as a special master to investigate whether lawyers representing the Justice and Interior departments committed ethical violations during the proceedings.The appointment follows a hearing on October 30, when Reyes raised concerns that government attorneys may have misrepresented the administration's plans to proceed with renovations at East Potomac Golf Links. The judge had previously issued an order temporarily blocking aspects of the redevelopment, but Trump subsequently indicated that work would begin immediately.Reuters also reported that Reyes was particularly concerned about the apparent contradiction between the president's public statements and the assurances presented by government lawyers in court.The judge had also expressed reservations about being asked to disregard the president's own announcements.The Guardian report states that Liu will examine the conduct of officials and legal representatives involved in the case, including those from the Department of Justice, Interior Department and National Park Service. The judge is allowing both sides to submit written responses to her proposed appointment before the next scheduled hearing.At the centre of the dispute is East Potomac Park, a historic public recreational area situated along the Potomac River. The Trump administration intends to close the golf course and park on November 15 as part of its redevelopment plans.The proposed transformation involves creating what the administration describes as a championship-level golf destination capable of hosting major tournaments and other significant sporting events, states the Guardian report.However, the project has faced opposition from preservation advocates and local residents. A lawsuit filed in February by the DC Preservation League and two Washington residents challenges the proposed reconstruction, arguing that it violates environmental protections and congressional legislation governing the preservation of the historic park.As The Guardian reported, more than 400 trees were cut down during the early stages of the controversy, raising questions about whether officials had proceeded with work despite assurances given to the court.Reyes subsequently issued an injunction temporarily preventing the government from removing or damaging additional trees. The order also requires the administration to provide 10 days' written notice before undertaking any irreversible changes to the golf course's existing features while the litigation continues.Liu brings considerable experience in federal law enforcement and the Justice Department. During Trump's first presidential term, she served as the US attorney for the District of Columbia, overseeing several high-profile matters referred to her office during special counsel Robert Mueller's investigation into alleged Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election, states Reuters report.She also supervised the criminal case involving Roger Stone, Trump's longtime friend and political adviser. Trump later nominated Liu for the position of associate attorney general, one of the Justice Department's senior leadership roles, although she eventually withdrew after encountering opposition in the Senate, the latest report claims.The Guardian noted that appointing a special master to investigate the conduct of participants in a court case is a significant development. Legal experts have suggested that such an investigation could potentially precede contempt-of-court proceedings, depending on what the inquiry establishes.The Interior Department has criticised Reyes's intervention, describing her as politically motivated and accusing her of obstructing the president's efforts to improve Washington's appearance, Reuters reported.The golf course redevelopment is part of Trump's broader effort to reshape the capital through architectural and construction projects. However, the dispute has placed the administration's approach to public land, environmental safeguards and compliance with judicial orders under scrutiny.For Reyes, the immediate question is whether government representatives accurately communicated the administration's intentions and complied with the court's directions. The investigation will now seek to establish who authorised the disputed work, what assurances were given and whether those assurances were truthful.What remains a relatively modest golf course redevelopment project has consequently developed into a much larger legal confrontation, with its outcome potentially carrying implications beyond the future of East Potomac Park. The findings could also influence how courts address disputes over government compliance with injunctions in future cases.Images Courtesy: Instagram/realdonaldtrump and Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP
Article Summary: US District Judge Ana Reyes appointed Jessie Liu, a former US attorney for the District of Columbia, as a special master to investigate government lawyers' conduct. The appointment follows a hearing on October 30, when Reyes raised concerns that government attorneys may have misrepresented the administration's plans to proceed with renovations at East Potomac Golf Links. The judge had previously issued an order temporarily blocking aspects of the redevelopment, but Trump subsequently indicated that work would begin immediately.

In separate fire incidents during Diwali, at least 12 family members lost their lives in Madhya Pradesh.





BHOPAL: At least 12 members of two families were killed in separate fire incidents in Madhya Pradesh’s Seoni and Katni districts a day after Diwali celebrations.In Seoni district, six members of a family were killed and four others injured after a massive fire broke out at a three-storey house belonging to a goldsmith in Chhapara town early Monday.The blaze erupted between 4am and 4.30am at the residence of Kundan Lal Soni, near a Jain temple in Mahavir Ward.10 people were present in the house when the fire broke out. Six of them died, while four were rescued, sub-divisional officer of police Apoorva Bhalavi told PTI.The deceased have been identified as Soni, 75, his wife Rajkumari, 65, Ritu, 42, Smriti, 40, Surya, 45, and Aditya, 16.The cause of the fire was not immediately known, officials said.In a separate incident in Katni district, six members of another family, including a two-month-old infant, died after a fire broke out at a crockery shop in a three-storey building in Barhi town around midnight, PTI reported.The deceased have been identified as Puran Agarwal, 77, who ran the shop, his wife Chandrakala, 74, daughter-in-law Poonam, granddaughters Arya, 14, and Anvi, 6, and a two-month-old infant.The fire quickly spread through the building, trapping family members inside. The infant died in his mother Poonam's arms, eyewitnesses said.The incident brought tears to the eyes of those present and spread grief across the town.The cause of the fire was not immediately clear.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: At least 12 members of two families were killed in separate fire incidents in Madhya Pradesh’s Seoni and Katni districts a day after Diwali celebrations. In Seoni district, six members of a family were killed and four others injured after a massive fire broke out at a three-storey house belonging to a goldsmith in Chhapara town early Monday.

Article Title: Chhattisgarh man kills cousin's 4-year-old son, removes kidneys, lungs and eyes; keeps organs in bucket
Article Text:
The accused regularly browsed social media for ways to earn quick money and subsequently developed the idea of extracting and selling organs





RAIPUR: A 27-year-old farm worker allegedly killed his cousin’s four-year-old son and removed organs from his body in Chhattisgarh’s Jashpur district, police said, claiming he conceived the plan while browsing social media for ways to make quick money.Basudev alias Tangnu, a resident of Chalni Gorrapath village, was arrested on Sunday after the child’s body was found concealed in a sack in a water-filled pit in Sanna village. Police said they recovered a bucket containing body parts, a knife, a shovel and his mobile phone.The purported motive rests on the accused’s statement during interrogation. Police have not disclosed evidence of contact with prospective buyers or any organ sale.According to police, Basudev stated during interrogation that after killing the child, he cut open the chest and abdomen with the same knife and removed a kidney, a lung and an eye, placing them in a plastic bucket.He then wrapped the body in a blanket and quilt, stuffed it into a sack and partly buried it in a water-filled pit in a field.Police said he separately concealed the bucket containing the body parts, along with the knife and a shovel, in a pit near a bamboo thicket.The child, Jitendra Ram, went missing on November 5. His father, Ramjeet Ram, 36, had moved to Sanna with his family about a year ago for work and lived in a hut near the Aamatchua river dam. Basudev, Ramjeet’s maternal cousin, frequently visited their home.According to the father’s complaint, Basudev took him and another acquaintance out for drinks around 9am on November 5. They later went towards the bus stand while Basudev left separately. When Ramjeet returned home, his son was missing. A witness told him he had seen the boy accompanying Basudev towards a hut in a field.After searching nearby villages and fields, Ramjeet and his relatives found the child’s body on November 7. It was wrapped in bedding, stuffed into a sack and partly covered with soil in a pit near a maize field.Police said Basudev, who grew vegetables on a farmer’s land and lived in a hut there, was dissatisfied with his earnings. During questioning, he purportedly told investigators that searching social media for ways to earn more had given him the idea of selling children’s organs.Investigators said he lured Jitendra away, took him to several places and later bought liquor and chicken. He allegedly gave the child alcohol and killed him with a knife after he fell asleep. Police said he then removed organs and concealed them in a bucket near a bamboo thicket.Basudev was arrested under BNS provisions relating to kidnapping, murder and disappearance of evidence, and sent to jail on judicial remand.
Article Summary: The child, Jitendra Ram, went missing on November 5. His father, Ramjeet Ram, 36, had moved to Sanna with his family about a year ago for work and lived in a hut near the Aamatchua river dam. Police said they recovered a bucket containing body parts, a knife, a shovel and his mobile phone.

Article Title: From north to south Kolkata, holy night least silent in recent times; hospitals reel under noise assault
Article Text:
A family enjoys Diwali on the terrace of an Amherst Street house





Kolkata: The city reeled under one of its worst noise assaults in recent times on Diwali night, as banned high-decibel crackers were burst across neighbourhoods well beyond the permitted 8pm-10pm window, with violations continuing into the early hours.Many localities had endured a similar spell of relentless cracker-bursting on the eve of Kali Puja , too.Eleven persons were arrested till 8.30pm on Sunday for bursting banned firecrackers. Around 50kg of illegal crackers were seized in the evening.The state pollution control board (PCB) had received 14 complaints by 9.30pm on Sunday, compared to only four on Saturday. Sources said the complaints were mostly from Haridevpur, Baguiati, Sonarpur, Phoolbagan, Kasba, Patuli, Golf Green and Taltala. A source said five PCB teams reported noise norm violations from across the city.Naba Datta, secretary of Sabuj Mancha, which works for the protection of the environment, said they had come across firecracker explosions on the RG Kar Medical College and Hospital premises on Sunday evening. “The noise levels were above 80 decibel at RG Kar and about 100 decibel at Dr BC Roy Children’s Hospital in the evening,” he said.The ambient noise level in hospitals should not cross 40 decibel after sundown.The noise pollution was compounded by a sharp fall in the city’s air quality. Hourly data from Saturday evening till Sunday morning showed Salt Lake’s PM2.5 level rising from 117 at 4pm to 330 at 11pm and peaking at 336 at 1am. It rose from 148 to 321 in Ballygunge and 159 to 326 in Jadavpur between 4pm and 11pm on Saturday. At Fort William, PM2.5 rose from 120 at 4pm on Saturday to 268 at 1am on Sunday. Rabindra Bharati University recorded a PM 2.5 level of 265 at 3pm on Saturday, while it reached 233 around 3am on Sunday at Victoria Memorial.PM2.5 between 201 and 300 is considered poor, and between 301 and 400, very poor.The barrage began soon after 8pm, intensified sharply after 10pm and continued all over the city till early hours. In many places, the sound demon started rearing its head even before 8pm. Chocolate bombs and other high-decibel fireworks were set off repeatedly in residential localities, including areas close to hospitals and other silent zones. While police action was visible in some pockets, residents across Kolkata said enforcement was lax.Among the worst-affected areas were New Alipore, Golf Green, Kalighat, Garia, Kasba and Sarsuna in south Kolkata; Taltala, Girish Park and Jorabagan in central Kolkata; and Kankurgachhi, Maniktala, Nagerbazar, Sinthee, Ultadanga, Lake Town, Bangur Avenue, Baguiati, Narkeldanga and Kestopur in the north and on northeastern fringes.Residents reported indiscriminate cracker bursting from upscale Wood Street, Theatre Road, Minto Park, Ballygunge Circular Road, Chakraberia and Lansdowne. Residents off EM Bypass, near Mukundapur, Salt Lake, Amherst Street, College Street, Kasba and Golf Green said they heard continuous sounds of firecracker explosions.“I live with elderly parents. A group of men was bursting chocolate bombs just outside my home. I pleaded with them to stop, but they paid no heed. I called police. By the time a jeep arrived, they had left. But they were back as soon as the cops left,” said Aditya Roy, a resident of Sinthee.“I take sleeping pills at night. Yet, for the past two nights, I was unable to sleep. On Saturday night, the torture continued till 3am,” said Rupsa Saha, who lives in an apartment beside Manipal Hospital in Dhakuria.The impact was also visible on animals and birds. “Dogs and cats were running helter-skelter, while frightened birds suddenly took flight after midnight as crackers continued exploding,” said Animesh Bhattacharya, a resident of Garia.Hospitals were not spared. On Kali Puja-eve, the ambient noise level reached 72.7 decibel at RG Kar hospital around midnight and 58.2 decibel at SSKM Hospital around 12.30am.Central Pollution Control Board prescribes an ambient noise ceiling of 45 decibel for residential areas between 10pm and 6am. Available estimates indicated that nighttime noise levels during the festive period ranged between 85 and 110-plus decibel during the period.
Article Summary: Eleven persons were arrested till 8.30pm on Sunday for bursting banned firecrackers. Around 50kg of illegal crackers were seized in the evening. The state pollution control board (PCB) had received 14 complaints on Sunday, compared to only four on Saturday.

Article Title: Diwali night ends in tragedy: 6 of family killed, 4 injured as fire engulfs goldsmith's 3-storey house in MP
Article Text:
A fire erupted early Monday morning at the residence of goldsmith Kundan Lal Soni in Seoni





SEONI: Six members of a family were killed and four others injured after a massive fire broke out at a three-storey house belonging to a goldsmith in Madhya Pradesh's Seoni district early on Monday, police said.The incident occurred between 4am and 4.30am, a day after Diwali, at the house of goldsmith Kundan Lal Soni near a Jain temple in Mahavir Ward in Chhapara town, news agency PTI reported.The deceased included three women and a minor.Ten people were present in the house at the time of the incident.The deceased have been identified as Kundan Lal Soni, 75, his wife Rajkumari Soni, 65, Ritu Soni, 42, Smriti Soni, 40, Surya Soni, 45, and Aditya Soni, 16, officials said.Six died, while four were evacuated, sub-divisional officer of police Apoorva Bhalavi, who was present at the spot, told PTI over the phone.He said the fire brigade and rescue teams later brought the blaze under control.The cause of the fire was not yet known.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: A fire broke out at a house belonging to a goldsmith in Madhya Pradesh's Seoni district early on Monday. The incident occurred between 4am and 4.30am, a day after Diwali, at the house of goldsmith Kundan Lal Soni near a Jain temple.

Article Title: 10-year-old boy dies after firecracker explodes in his hand while bursting crackers in Delhi
Article Text:
Police are investigating the type of explosive involved and the circumstances leading to the incident (Image used for representational purpose)

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: A 10-year-old boy died after a firecracker exploded in his hand while he was bursting crackers in Delhi’s Narela, police said on Monday.Police are investigating the type of explosive involved and the circumstances leading to the incident.According to Delhi Police, the child was injured when the firecracker exploded in his hand.He was rushed to hospital but later succumbed to his injuries.According to news agency ANI, police have launched an investigation to identify the type of firecracker involved and determine the circumstances leading to the explosion.The investigation is underway to establish the sequence of events leading to the child's death.Further details about the incident are awaited.
Article Summary: A 10-year-old boy died after a firecracker exploded in his hand while he was bursting crackers in Delhi’s Narela. He was rushed to hospital but later succumbed to his injuries. Police are investigating the type of explosive involved and the circumstances leading to the incident.

Article Title: Serial killings in Bengaluru: Indushekhar’s brother had faced murder charges in 2018; died in prison
Article Text:
Indushekhar is the younger brother of S Ramesh, a key figure named in a 2018 investigation that exposed a chilling murder tied to a major land scam.

What had happened?





BENGALURU: As investigators continue to uncover details surrounding the serial killings that have shaken Bengaluru, fresh links have emerged connecting the prime accused, S Indushekhar, to a troubling family history of high-profile crime.Indushekhar is the younger brother of S Ramesh , a key figure named in a 2018 investigation that exposed a chilling murder tied to a major land scam.However, Ramesh died of illness as an undertrial prisoner in Bengaluru central prison. Currently in police custody, Indushekhar faces charges of killing seven persons, including his wife, over suspected domestic and property issues.On Sept 18, 2018, a security guard named Venkataswamy walked into Avalahalli police station in tears, reporting that his 40-year-old wife, Sudharani , had set herself on fire. Just seven hours after he arrived, police registered a murder case following a formal complaint from Sudharani’s father, Muniyappa. By Sept 25, the investigation had uncovered the conspiracy: Sudharani’s death was directly linked to a multi-crore land scam and the murder of an elderly man.The masterminds behind the plot were realtor S Ramesh and his associates Shankarappa, S Krishnamurthy, and M Keshavamurthy. Ramesh had identified a lucrative plot of land in Belathur valued at around Rs 12 to 15 crore. The land belonged to a man named Nanjappa, whose whereabouts were completely unknown.To seize the property, the group enlisted a stamp vendor to forge ownership documents. They recruited a 90-year-old man named Venkataramanappa to impersonate Nanjappa at the Banaswadi sub-registrar’s office and executed a fake will in Ramesh’s name.The gang struck a deal with a physician, who agreed to issue a fake death certificate under Nanjappa’s name once presented with a corpse. To secure a body, the conspirators targeted an elderly man named Krishnappa at a bus stop in Kolar. They lured him to Bengaluru under the pretext of offering him a higher-paying job. On Sept 14, they administered a fatal overdose of medication to him, causing severe gastroenteritis that killed him the following day.The gang then hired Venkataswamy to take the victim’s ashes to Srirangapatna and perform the final rites for a financial payout. Suspicious of the secret ritual, Sudharani repeatedly questioned her husband until Venkataswamy confessed the entire murder plot to her. Fearing exposure, Venkataswamy informed Ramesh and the gang, leading to Sudharani’s murder.
Article Summary: Indushekhar is the younger brother of S Ramesh, a key figure named in a 2018 investigation that exposed a chilling murder tied to a major land scam. Currently in police custody, Indus hekhar faces charges of killing seven persons, including his wife, over suspected domestic and property issues.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu records 1,116 firecracker injuries on Diwali; 131 remain hospitalised
Article Text:
During Diwali celebrations, a total of 1,116 individuals sought medical treatment for firecracker injuries in Tamil Nadu.





CHENNAI: A total of 1,116 people received medical treatment for firecracker-related injuries across Tamil Nadu during Diwali oil celebrations on Sunday, while the Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services control room received 160 emergency calls, including 104 concerning fires caused by firecrackers.According to the department, the remaining 56 calls were related to other fire incidents.Of the 1,116 people injured, 985 received treatment and returned home.They included 597 men, 98 women and 290 children.The remaining 131 people, comprising 103 men, nine women and 19 children, continued to receive treatment in hospitals, the fire department said.
Article Summary: A total of 1,116 people received medical treatment for firecracker-related injuries across Tamil Nadu during Diwali oil celebrations. Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services control room received 160 emergency calls, including 104 concerning fires caused by firecrackers. The remaining 56 calls were related to other fire incidents.

Article Title: Parth meets Sharad Pawar twice in 2 days, NCP leaders seek to revive merger talks
Article Text:
Parth Pawar met Sharad Pawar for two consecutive days, raising speculation about a potential merger of NCP factions (File photo)

Praful Patel: Will meet Sharad Pawar on Nov 10





PUNE: Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar’s elder son and Rajya Sabha member Parth Pawar on Sunday met his granduncle and NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar for the second consecutive day at the latter’s Mumbai residence amid renewed speculation that a disgruntled section of NCP was attempting to revive merger talks with the rival faction.Parth held discussions with the veteran leader for nearly two hours, fuelling speculation about a possible reunion of the two NCP factions.The two had a nearly two-hour meeting on Saturday also, followed by a separate meeting between Sharad Pawar and senior NCP (SP) leaders in the evening.The second meeting, attended by Jayant Patil, Shashikant Shinde, Amol Kolhe, Anil Deshmukh and Jitendra Awhad, lasted nearly three hours. Most of these leaders were also involved in merger talks with late Ajit Pawar , with Patil leading the discussions.After meeting Sharad Pawar, Kolhe and Awhad told reporters that there was no discussion about a merger and that the NCP (SP) leaders had met their party chief only to inquire about his health. Pawar was discharged from hospital on Saturday.NCP national working president Praful Patel said he would meet Sharad Pawar after November 10 in Mumbai, adding to the buzz surrounding the proposed merger.Patel had met him on Thursday when the veteran leader was admitted to Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital.The meeting fuelled speculation about a possible merger after a video surfaced on social media showing the two discussing certain issues.Speaking to reporters in Gondia on Sunday, Patel denied discussing politics during the hospital visit. He said they briefly discussed political developments but did not engage in any detailed political discussions.“A hospital is not the place for political discussions and I did not want to hold any such talks there. I only told Pawar saheb that I would meet him at his residence in Mumbai after Nov 10 and discuss things. But that does not mean we will discuss only politics,” Patel said, adding that Sharad Pawar was a senior leader and everyone wanted him to continue guiding the state and the country.Earlier, seven NCP leaders, Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal, Dilip Walse Patil, Hasan Mushrif, Dhananjay Munde and Samir Bhujbal, met Union home minister Amit Shah in Delhi reportedly without the knowledge of Parth and party president Sunetra Pawar, fuelling speculation about growing differences within the party.A senior NCP leader who attended the meeting told TOI on the condition of anonymity that several senior functionaries were unhappy with Parth, alleging that he had repeatedly taken key decisions without consulting the party leaders. This, the leader said, had led to growing resentment among senior leaders.The discontent reportedly intensified following the appointments of Umesh Patil as the party’s national chief spokesperson and Zeeshan Siddiqui as the Mumbai unit president.According to NCP sources, neither appointment was discussed within the party and several senior leaders were not even aware of the decisions. Chhagan Bhujbal publicly admitted that he learnt about the new appointments through media reports.Earlier on Friday, state NCP president Sunil Tatkare said the merger of the two factions would have taken place in Feb had former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar been alive. After Ajit Pawar’s death, Tatkare and Patel both had denied reports of merger talks between Ajit Pawar and NCP (SP) leaders.The back-to-back meetings between Parth and Sharad Pawar, the meeting with NCP (SP) leaders, coupled with Patel’s announcement of a meeting after November 10, have once again brought the possibility of a reunion of the two NCP factions into focus.Against this backdrop, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday said the two factions were independent entities and were free to take their own decisions.“It would be inappropriate for us to comment on the matter. If they (NCP factions) decide to take any such steps, they will consult us,” he said.
Article Summary: Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar’s elder son and Rajya Sabha member Parth Pawar on Sunday met his granduncle and NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar for the second consecutive day. Parth held discussions with the veteran leader for nearly two hours, fuelling speculation about a possible reunion of the two NCP factions.

Article Title: Drought-hit Karnataka cannot afford polluted rivers: Experts warn of sewage contamination and shrinking oxygen levels
Article Text:
Karnataka is grappling with severe river pollution caused by untreated sewage from various sources (file photo used for representation)

Arkavathi vs other rivers

Drains turned into sewage channels

Water quality classes

Make polluters pay for clean rivers

Key no from the report

Funding issues, drains hamper





BENGALURU: A state grappling with drought can ill afford to let its rivers become repositories for untreated sewage. Yet, Karnataka’s latest water-quality assessment presents a troubling picture: at some monitoring points, pollution is severe enough to leave little or no oxygen in the water, while bacterial counts run into lakhs.The Karnataka State Pollution Control Board’s August 2026 assessment covers 66 monitoring locations across 14 identified polluted stretches.The readings show that pollution is not confined to a few prominent waterways but extends across multiple river stretches. Data for rivers beyond the Dakshina Pinakini and Arkavathi, two of the most affected rivers with high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) and high faecal-coliform counts, also raise concern.High (BOD) indicates that microorganisms need more oxygen to break down organic pollution, leaving less dissolved oxygen available for aquatic life.High faecal-colifor m counts indicate contamination by faecal matter and warn of the possible presence of disease-causing pathogens.Experts point out that with water already scarce, long-term plans to protect its quality should be as critical as securing its supply while framing policies.KC Subhash Chandra, a hydrogeologist, says that Bengaluru’s natural drains, or rajakaluves, have become conduits for sewage, with discharges from residential areas flowing into lakes.These flows are perennial, yet pollution levels went unexamined for years, while sewage treatment remained lacking. The problem extends beyond Bengaluru. Townships across Karnataka generate pollution through human activity.Industrial discharges into drains worsen the situation and risk groundwater contamination. Rules prohibit industrial pollution in natural drains and groundwater, but strict action is needed to prevent such discharges.Industries, including textile, lead and battery units, must keep sewage and effluents out of natural drains and treat them to tertiary, potable-level standards. Otherwise, pollution will continue.Regular monitoring of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD) and dissolved oxygen (DO) can establish the extent of contamination. Recent fish deaths in lakes should serve as a warning. Sewage inflows reduce dissolved oxygen, while oxygen demand rises.Until discharges are stopped and treated, Bengaluru’s lakes will remain vulnerable.Vishwanath S, who is a Water conservation expert, says that industrial pollution must also be stopped through effluent treatment plants, ensuring no industrial discharge enters rivers. Domestic sewage is greater in volume, but industrial effluents have a greater impact. Filing cases is the least that can be done.Peenya industrial area, which pollutes the Arkavathi, doesn’t have a single functional common effluent treatment plant of scale. We need a long-term plan and, until then, must recognise that rivers will remain polluted.The question is where the money will come from. The principle must be that polluters pay.Every household & apartment discharging sewage must pay for its collection, conveyance and treatment. Unless we get the pricing of water and wastewater right, institutions responsible for managing them won’t have funds to tackle pollution and we’ll keep repeating the ritual every year: a report flags pollution, the board issues notices, and pollution continues.We must address the root of the problem by establishing a system to collect the money needed to treat wastewater. That’s a difficult political question because nobody wants to raise water prices or charge for sewage collection and treatment.Action plans have been prepared for all identified polluted river stretches in Karnataka, but gaps in sewage infrastructure, funding constraints and delays in coordination continue to hamper Karnataka State Pollution Control Board’s (KSPCB) clean up efforts.Untreated sewage is the primary source of river pollution, a senior official said. Restoring water quality requires sewage treatment plants (STPs) along rivers, but inadequate underground drainage networks remain a hurdle.“Laying pipes needs a large budget, and the state can’t release funds all at once,” the official said, adding that projects have to be taken up in phases, with priority given to cities like Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru.The official was hopeful of completing works in the next two years. Coordination among around 270 urban local bodies and panchayats presents another challenge.Most STPs have to be established by these bodies, requiring clearances, budgets and permissions. While almost all cities have STPs, some have been discontinued.In Bengaluru, most identified polluted stretches are along the Arkavathi, while many of Karnataka’s polluted stretches are near Belagavi, which has numerous riverbanks, the official said.The board has also stepped up enforcement.It has filed around 40–42 criminal cases under the Water Act against polluters, the official said. Several of the cases are pending before district magistrate courts. Earlier, action largely involved fines, but the board is now pursuing criminal cases as well.The KSPCB also conducts awareness programmes, particularly during festivals, urging people not to dump waste into rivers.Following national green tribunal and high court orders, urban local bodies have received pollution-control funding more actively in recent years, though allocations are being made progressively.
Article Summary: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board’s August 2026 assessment covers 66 monitoring locations across 14 identified polluted stretches. The readings show that pollution is not confined to a few prominent waterways but extends across multiple river stretches. Industry, including textile, lead and battery units, must keep sewage and effluents out of natural drains and treat them to tertiary, potable-level standards.
